ledger.claim: POL-RD-22 measures the deviation from the platform's recorded distances, not from the GPS trace: trip_record.actual_distance_km 11.4 km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km 9.9 km is 1.50 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance, and the 47-fix trace measures only 9.584 km precisely because, as POL-RD-22 says, a sparse trace understates a route's length and is not used to re-measure. The tolerance limbs of the matrix are therefore closed and the deviation is a real one of 1.50 km.

The driver did give in-app notice before deviating — MSG-05008-003 at 19:34:22 ('KPE very jam after Sims Way, I come out at Sims Ave and go Aljunied ok?') precedes the route_deviation_detected at 19:37:02 — but POL-RD-21 makes a deviation 'agreed' only where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment, and this chat log records the opposite: MSG-05008-004 at 19:34:52, 'No need, pls just stay on KPE, I don't mind the jam', and MSG-05008-005 at 19:38:22, 'Eh I said no need already, why still exit'. Row (a) of POL-RD-24 — the only row under which a deviation over 1 km attracts no refund — requires the rider to be informed AND to have agreed; the agreement limb fails on the platform's own log, and the rider's objection is not a mere assertion in her statement but is corroborated word-for-word in the record.

With row (a) unavailable and the deviation over the 1 km tolerance, the rows that can apply are (b) and (d), and each of them returns the excess distance fare: 1.50 km times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd 0.72, with no surge, equals 1.08 SGD, which is exactly the figure built into the policy's excess_distance_fare formula. That is also exactly the 1.08 SGD already refunded (refund_issued_sgd 1.08, payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED). The rider is left carrying nothing for the deviation the driver took against her express instruction.

Even if the judge treats the LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-05008-01 — HEAVY_TRAFFIC on the KPE, 'after Sims Way exit', towards TPE, valid 19:09 to 20:19, overlapping the 19:29-19:52 trip window — as satisfying POL-RD-23 on the recommended route, justification does not convert a refused reroute into an agreed one. A finding of traffic justification opens rows (b) and (c) only; (c) is closed by the 1.50 km deviation, so on a deviation over 1 km the justified branch (b) and the unjustified branch (d) both refund the excess distance fare. The rider's money position does not depend on how the traffic question is resolved.

If the judge reads POL-RD-24 as exhaustive and holds that this configuration — traffic-justified, rider informed, rider objecting, deviation over 1 km, the very situation the clause's closing sentence names — fits no lettered row, the case escalates under POL-GEN-26. Escalation does not put the rider in a worse position: under POL-GEN-03 ESCALATE is terminal, no monetary outcome issues and the amount is held, so the 1.08 SGD is not collected from the rider pending human review, and the refund already paid is not clawed back in the meantime.

The contested amount is 1.08 SGD, below the 10.00 SGD band, so under POL-GEN-22 the AI ruling is final at any confidence, and POL-RD-25's 0.80 bar is met on a record whose artifacts are all COMPLETE at weight 1.0; no fraud flag stands against either party (driver_profile.fraud_flags 0, and the authority block records fraud_flags 0), so POL-GEN-22's 0.95 bar is not engaged and the case can be finally ruled rather than deferred. POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is not applied — route_deviation.thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false — and in any event the deviation is 1.50 km, under that ceiling.

No field on either party's profile may ground a finding about this trip except the two POL-GEN-01 names — fraud_flags (POL-GEN-22) and no_show_cancellations_30d (POL-NS-25) — and neither of those bears on a route deviation; every other profile field is context only. The outcome here rests on the trip record, the chat log and the fare ledger, and nothing on the rider's snapshot can be used to discount her account of a deviation she asked the driver in writing not to make.

The reroute is traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. EV-ADVIS-05008-01 is an LTA TRAFFIC_ADVISORY of type HEAVY_TRAFFIC - a type the policy's traffic_justification_types maps onto 'congestion' - for the Kallang-Paya Lebar Expressway (KPE) towards TPE after Sims Way exit, valid 19:09:23 to 20:19:23, and it therefore overlaps the trip window 19:29:23 to 19:52:23 (overlaps_trip_window true). The recommended route recorded in EV-TRIP-05008 runs via the KPE, and the trip record's own route_deviation_detected event places the exit at 'KPE / Sims Way exit' - the same road and the same location the advisory names. The advisory's derived block leaves intersects_route undetermined for the Judge rather than deciding it, but the record's own road and location labels put the congestion on the very segment the driver was driving at the time, so POL-RD-23's condition is satisfied and this was not a discretionary detour.

The driver gave the notice POL-RD-21 requires, and gave it before the point of deviation. MSG-05008-003 was sent at 19:34:22, delivered at 19:34:23 and read at 19:35:00, and it states both the reason and the intended alternative: 'Miss, KPE very jam after Sims Way, I come out at Sims Ave and go Aljunied ok? Faster.' That is the brief reason POL-RD-21 asks for, and it is in-app chat, which POL-RD-21 accepts without any call recording. The trace's first off-route fix is the Sims Avenue fix at 19:36:53 and the trip record's deviation event is at 19:37:02, so the notice preceded the deviation by over two minutes. POL-RD-21 obliges the driver to inform the rider of a traffic reroute; it does not oblige him to obtain consent, and consent is a separate element that only row (a) of POL-RD-24 turns on.

The deviation is 1.50 km and is over tolerance. EV-TRIP-05008 records actual_distance_km 11.4 and optimal_distance_km 9.9, and POL-RD-22 makes the deviation their difference - 1.50 km - measured from the platform's recorded distances, not from the trace, because a sparse trace understates a route's length (the trace's own 9.584 km would understate it here). The 1.0 km tolerance in POL-RD-22 is therefore exceeded, and the 2.0 km AI limb in POL-RD-25 is expressly not applied (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied false, EV-TRIP-05008 derived), so nothing on the distance side of the policy closes this case.

Neither refund row of POL-RD-24 is met, so the 1.08 SGD has no row to stand on. Row (b) refunds the excess distance fare where the reroute is traffic-justified but the rider was not informed - the rider was informed by in-app chat before the deviation (MSG-05008-003 at 19:34:22, read 19:35:00), so (b) fails. Row (d) refunds where the reroute is not traffic-justified - the LTA HEAVY_TRAFFIC advisory on the KPE at the trip time justifies it, so (d) fails. The 1.08 SGD in EV-FARE-05008 is exactly the excess distance fare (deviation_km 1.50 x per_km_rate_sgd 0.72, no surge applied), and the matrix pays that figure only in rows (b) and (d). The interim recovery of it from the driver's earnings should not be finalised on this record.

The case fits no row of POL-RD-24, and the clause itself says what happens then: 'A case that fits no row (for example, informed but the rider objected) is escalated under POL-GEN-26.' That is this case precisely - traffic-justified, the driver informed the rider before the point of deviation, and the rider answering in MSG-05008-004 'No need, pls just stay on KPE, I don't mind the jam' and in MSG-05008-005 'Eh I said no need already, why still exit'. Row (a)'s 'informed and agreed' is therefore not made out, and rows (c) and (e) cannot apply to a 1.50 km deviation. The escalation is directed by the matrix on its own terms, not manufactured out of any gap in the record.

On the fare state in EV-FARE-05008 - payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 1.08, recovered from the driver's earnings pending review - the values POL-RD-24 licenses do not treat the driver alike, and POL-GEN-03 fixes their meaning. NO_ACTION is party-relative and leaves the present state standing, which here is the very refund the driver contests; PARTIAL_REFUND returns part of the trip's charge to the rider and would confirm the same 1.08 against him. ESCALATE issues no monetary outcome and holds the amount for the human reviewer, and it is the only licensed disposition that does not close the money against the driver while the 'informed but the rider objected' question is unresolved.

Neither side's snapshot carries a fraud flag - EV-DPROF-05008 records driver_profile.fraud_flags 0 and EV-RPROF-05008 carries no fraud flag field - so POL-GEN-22's 0.95 uplift is not engaged and the confidence this case is held to is not raised against the driver. Beyond that single field, POL-GEN-01 makes every other field on either profile context only: it may inform how closely a party's assertions are scrutinised, but it may never establish a fact about this trip or decide it. The rider's history cannot substitute for the chat log, the advisory or the recorded distances on this trip.

The record is complete on every artifact this claim set relies on: EV-TRIP-05008, EV-GPS-05008, EV-CHAT-05008, EV-FARE-05008, EV-RPROF-05008, EV-DPROF-05008 and EV-ADVIS-05008-01 each carry status COMPLETE and weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes fired. POL-GEN-02's discount rule therefore depresses nothing, the GPS trace at 47 fixes and 100 per cent coverage needs no disclosure caveat, and the escalation sought here is the escalation POL-RD-24 directs for a case that fits no row - not an escalation for a fact the record cannot establish.

ruling.explanation:
The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and the drafts did not agree, so no ruling was carried and the dispute is escalated. Each draft proposed:
- draft 1 (sampled): ESCALATE, amount_sgd null, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
- draft 2 (sampled): abstained -- DRAFT_CLAUSE_UNRESOLVED: 'POL-NS-22' does not resolve in the loaded policy; DRAFT_CLAUSE_UNRESOLVED: 'POL-NS-24' does not resolve in the loaded policy; DRAFT_CLAUSE_UNRESOLVED: 'POL-NS-25' does not resolve in the loaded policy
- draft 3 (sampled): abstained -- DRAFT_CLAUSE_UNRESOLVED: 'POL-NS-24' does not resolve in the loaded policy; DRAFT_CLAUSE_UNRESOLVED: 'POL-NS-25' does not resolve in the loaded policy; DRAFT_CLAUSE_UNRESOLVED: 'POL-NS-22' does not resolve in the loaded policy
- draft 4 (position_swapped): ESCALATE, amount_sgd null, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
At most 2 of 2 valid drafts agreed and 3 were needed. The best supported answer is not published as a ruling: a ruling has to be the panel's, not one draft's.
